Brahma. The creator god of the Hindu trinity, responsible for bringing the universe into being at the start of each cosmic cycle.

Brahma is the first member of the Trimurti and is responsible for creation and the birth of all beings. He is depicted with four heads and four arms, with each head facing a cardinal direction. This symbolizes his omniscience and ability to see all things. He holds sacred texts—the Vedas—in one hand and a mala, a string of prayer beads, in another. These represent knowledge and spiritual practice.

His consort is Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, arts, and learning. She emerges from his mind. In Hindu cosmology, Brahma is associated with the cosmic egg, the Hiranyagarbha, from which all creation emerged.

Despite his supreme role in creation, Brahma is worshipped less frequently than Vishnu or Shiva. Relatively few temples are dedicated solely to him. In Vedic times, rituals and sacrifices were thought to sustain his creative powers and maintain the universe.

The Brahma Sutras are philosophical texts that attempt to explain the relationship between Brahman—ultimate reality itself—and the created universe. Through these texts, Hindu philosophy explores how the absolute manifests as all things that exist.
